text:
Maria: Hey — ran into a weird Terraform failure after merging my PR. CI apply fails during the KMS grant create with AccessDenied (iam:PassRole / kms:CreateGrant). I added an aws_kms_grant for the IRSA role. Snippet from the module:
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "irsa_grant" {
  key_id           = aws_kms_key.svc_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.irsa_role.arn
  operations       = ["Encrypt", "Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```
CI error: `Error: Error creating IAM RolePolicyAttachment: AccessDenied` — anyone seen this when using IRSA + grants?

AJ: Quick thought: terraform needs kms:CreateGrant on the principal doing the apply. If the key policy is locked down (only admins/root), CI role can't create grants. Are we running TF with the org CI principal or a deploy user?

Maria: CI runner is org-ci-role. The key policy is currently the default we applied (only account root + service account role in statements later). I expected creating aws_kms_grant in the same apply to work.

Devon: Two common gotchas: 1) CreateGrant requires permission in both IAM and the key policy (kms:CreateGrant). 2) If the key policy doesn't allow the CI principal to manage grants, CreateGrant will 403 even if your IAM user has kms:CreateGrant. Check the key policy statements.

Kai: Also watch ordering: if you create the key and then immediately create the grant, the key policy might not yet include the CI role (if you're also updating the key policy in the same apply). Terraform can try CreateGrant before the policy update is realized. I usually add an explicit depends_on from the grant to the key policy update resource.

Maria: Good call. In our module the key policy is defined inline on the key resource, so maybe TF is doing the grant create during the plan/apply before the key policy change is active. Any example depends_on to reference?

AJ: Something like:
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_key" "svc_key" { ... }
resource "aws_kms_key_policy" "svc_policy" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.svc_key.key_id
  policy = jsonencode(local.kms_policy)
}
resource "aws_kms_grant" "irsa_grant" {
  depends_on = [aws_kms_key_policy.svc_policy]
  key_id = aws_kms_key.svc_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.irsa_role.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "Encrypt"]
}
```
That forces the policy to be applied first.

Devon: Also check that the grantee_principal is correct for IRSA. When the pod calls KMS, the caller principal will be the assumed role (role ARN). Using the IAM role ARN is fine, but if the service account role is created in another stack, ensure TF knows the correct ARN (use data.aws_iam_role if cross-stack).

Maria: Oh — our chart sets the service account in a separate k8s/helm deploy. The role ARN was hardcoded in the terraform var (we merged a change). Could be a mismatch.

Kai: Helm values check — make sure chart values for the svc set `kmsKeyArn` to the new key. Otherwise the app will keep using the old key and secrets controller will fail. Also external-secrets needs proper permissions.

Maria: There's also a merge conflict that touched the key policy JSON (two PRs modified the same statement). The plan shows policy diff but then CreateGrant fails. I suspect the apply user can't both overwrite policy and create grants in the same transaction.

AJ: In that case: 1) fix the policy merge so the final policy includes CI principal kms:CreateGrant if you want CI to create grants, or 2) have a separate, privileged step (admin approval/manual apply) that creates the grants after the policy change. For immediate unblock pick (2).

Devon: Another pattern: don't create aws_kms_grant in CI for IRSA-managed pods. Instead, author the key policy to allow the IAM role ARNs (or the AWS account:root) to use the key; grants are often ephemeral and cause lifecycle headaches. If you can express it in key policy, it's simpler.

InfraBot: Deployment pipeline: https://ci.internal.redwood/teams/infra/pipelines/4823 — last failed step: terraform-apply (runner: org-ci-role). Logs attached.

Maria: Thanks everyone. Plan: I'll revert the grant creation from this PR and open a follow-up to either: add CI principal to key policy (if security ok) OR request a manual apply by infra-sre to create the grant after policy merge. I'll also update Helm values to pull kmsKeyArn from the infra outputs instead of hardcoding.

AJ: Sounds good — ping me on the follow-up PR. If you go manual-apply route, add an apply runner with an admin token and a short note in the PR so folks aren't surprised.

Kai: I can check the helm values quick — ping me the chart/values file and I'll do a quick pass.

Maria: Will do. tagging @AJ @Kai for review on the follow-up. Thanks :thumbsup:
